bottom_line: Stocks took a hard hit. The Dow fell below 50,000 for the first time since June, and even Anthropic's huge stock market debut didn't stop the slide in tech. Meanwhile the Fed, the people who set interest rates, is openly talking about raising rates because prices are still rising too fast.

stories.title: Big AI debut, market still fell
stories.real: Anthropic, the company behind Claude, started trading at a $1.8 trillion value after raising more than $100B, and its shares jumped 27% on day one. The rest of the market sank anyway: the Dow lost about 1,100 points, the Nasdaq dropped 2.2%, and SoftBank fell over 16% in Asia as the AI sell-off spread.

stories.title: The Fed is leaning toward hikes
stories.real: Several Fed officials say rates need to go up. Their own meeting notes point to a hike in December, and J.P. Morgan expects hikes at the next three meetings. Goolsbee said inflation is 'way higher' than the Fed's 2% goal, and Jefferson said the AI building boom is pushing prices up. They agree rates should rise but disagree on how fast.
stories.you: Loans, credit cards and mortgages could get more expensive, not cheaper.

stories.title: Chip makers in trouble over China
stories.real: California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, sent Nvidia a subpoena (a legal demand for records) in a probe into AI chips going to China, right after CEO Jensen Huang resigned. Rep. Mast says the Commerce Department approved sales of more than 879,000 AI chips to Chinese companies. AMD closed down over 7% after a short seller (someone who profits when a stock falls) claimed its firmware showed up at a blacklisted Chinese company. AMD says it follows U.S. law.
stories.you: Nvidia and AMD are huge parts of many tech and index funds, so their legal problems can show up in your account.

stories.title: Everyday costs still squeezing people
stories.real: Fuel costs are soaring. Walmart raised its outlook and says it's trying to keep prices low anyway. People report struggling with everything from gas to groceries. Slightly more people are filing for unemployment aid, though the number is still low historically, and the Fed told its own regional staff to expect smaller raises in 2027.
stories.you: Jobs are mostly holding up, but your paycheck may not stretch as far, and big raises look less likely.

stories.title: New law to protect older investors
stories.real: Both the House and Senate passed the Financial Exploitation Prevention Act, which aims to protect vulnerable investors from fraud. Separately, the Senate passed a permitting bill backed by the AI and energy industries, but it still has to clear the House.
stories.you: If you have older parents or grandparents with savings, they may get more legal protection against scams.
